title: Separate optional Management Console from Usage collection
scope: Introduce an explicitly started, read-only Management Console that reads canonical state and retained telemetry without a writer lease, Codex attachment, or background repository polling.
Introduce a separate on-demand Usage Collector that owns telemetry writes and Codex observation without serving the Management Console; keep managed-local collection experimental and non-default.
Preserve Temple Core delivery, existing telemetry, private-viewer safety, and unknown usage semantics when neither optional process is running.
acceptance_criteria: Temple initialization, lifecycle commands, and delivery remain complete with no Console or Collector process installed or running.

The optional Console can run concurrently with a telemetry writer, starts no Codex Provider or repository polling loop, exposes read-only routes only, and refreshes from bounded file-change invalidation.
The on-demand Usage Collector starts no HTTP listener, preserves local telemetry on shutdown, reports truthful on-demand status, and is the process used by the experimental managed-local service.
Focused runtime tests, full verification, live local measurement, documentation checks, and Independent QA pass at an exact revision.
overlap_resolution: WI-0033 remains an earlier control-plane specification item with no claim; WI-0100 owns only the optional Console and Collector process separation and preserves its unrelated scope.
WI-0086 remains the blocked public-release umbrella; WI-0100 performs no publication, visibility, tag, release, or hosting-setting action.
WI-0094 retains later snapshot performance optimization; WI-0100 establishes the process boundary first and does not claim that optimization complete.
WI-0097 owns adaptive repository onboarding; WI-0100 starts from its candidate and does not change repository-integration behavior.
WI-0098 remains the reviewed adaptive-onboarding implementation; WI-0100 preserves its CLI and ADR-index content while adding a separate command surface.
WI-0099 owns Node.js 24 and bounded-CI policy; WI-0100 starts from candidate 36703f3, preserves its changes, and limits shared docs/adr/README.md edits to adding ADR-0044 after ADR-0043.
